_comment: Semantic-correctness evaluation set. Questions and expected facts were written by hand from the fixture source, independently of any model output. Automatic checks are keyword/evidence heuristics that flag answers for review; they are NOT a measure of semantic accuracy. Semantic accuracy is only what a human reviewer records.

items.architecture: layered Python service (FastAPI route -> domain function -> helpers)
items.question: What happens when a user logs in via POST /login?

expected_facts.fact: The route handler login_route delegates to login()
login() creates the account through Account.create
The password is checked by check_password, which calls Account.validate
A token is produced by issue_token, which calls sign

plausible_wrong.claim: Sessions or tokens are stored in Redis

correct.text: POST /login is handled by login_route in svc/api/app.py, which calls login(name, password). login() normalises the name via Account.create, then calls check_password, which relies on Account.validate and a minimum password length; if the check fails it raises ValueError('denied'). Otherwise issue_token(account) returns sign(account.name).

plausible_wrong.text: POST /login validates the password with bcrypt and issues a JWT that is cached in Redis.

items.question: Which code could be affected if Account.validate changes?

expected_facts.fact: login depends on it transitively, so POST /login is potentially affected
The admin route is potentially affected through Admin.promote

correct.text: Account.validate is called directly by check_password and by Admin.promote. login calls check_password, so POST /login (login_route) is potentially affected, and GET /admin/{name} (admin_route) is potentially affected through Admin.promote. The test test_login also exercises login.

plausible_wrong.text: Changing Account.validate affects only the tests; the Go Store.Add method also calls it.

items.question: Which database does this service use in production?

correct.text: The analysed code contains no database client or configuration, so the production database cannot be determined from this snapshot.

plausible_wrong.text: The service stores its data in Redis, as described in the README.

items.architecture: Flask app with factory function and abstract repository
items.question: How does GET /items/<sku> produce its response?

expected_facts.fact: It builds the service with make_service
InventoryService.lookup fetches the record from the repository
The repository is the in-memory MemoryRepo
The record is formatted by _present into sku/qty

plausible_wrong.claim: Records are read from a SQL database
The endpoint is implemented in Express

correct.text: get_item in inv/web.py calls make_service(repo), which returns an InventoryService around the module-level MemoryRepo. InventoryService.lookup calls self.repo.fetch(sku) — MemoryRepo.fetch reads an in-memory dict — and _present converts the tuple into {sku, qty}, which jsonify returns.

plausible_wrong.text: get_item queries the SQL database through SQLAlchemy and returns the row.

items.architecture: Go net/http server with constructor function
items.question: What does the invctl Go program expose and how is it started?

correct.text: main creates the server with server.New(":8080"), registers /health with http.HandleFunc pointing at Server.Health (which writes 200 OK), and starts it with Server.Run, which logs and calls http.ListenAndServe on the address.

plausible_wrong.text: invctl is a Gin application that exposes a gRPC health service.

items.architecture: Spring controller with constructor injection and field initializer
items.question: How is the stock level returned by StockController.level computed?

plausible_wrong.claim: Stock levels are read from a database

correct.text: StockController.level calls clock.tick() on the Clock created by the field initializer and returns ledger.balance(sku). StockLedger.balance computes total(sku) - reserved(sku), which are constants 10 and 2 in this snapshot.

plausible_wrong.text: level loads the stock row from a JPA repository and caches the result.

items.question: What authentication does the catalog API require?

correct.text: No authentication was found: catalog/src/server.ts registers GET /catalog without any middleware, so the analysed code does not require authentication.

plausible_wrong.text: The catalog API requires a bearer JWT validated by middleware.
